timeline.title: The launch decision we make measurable
timeline.narration: Curve Covenant helps a launch creator choose a bonding curve before deploying an xStock paired token. The product starts with a concrete decision: should a creator prioritize a smaller opening price jump, or a lower share of tokens going to early buyers? Those outcomes can conflict. Our initial customer hypothesis is launchpad teams and creators who need to review that choice.

timeline.title: The evidence changes the story
timeline.narration: Under an identical whale schedule, the long curve reduces the first price jump from three hundred eleven percent to two hundred thirty nine percent. But early buyers receive two point five three percentage points more of gross buy output. The long curve also ends at a higher price. We show the cost alongside the benefit. This is a hypothetical result, not a promise of fairness or market performance.

timeline.title: From comparison to the exact launch
timeline.narration: The product runs retail, whale, selling pressure, and graduation scenarios. Every transaction updates the next state, and sellers cannot sell tokens they do not hold. Builders inspect price paths, fees, costs, and reserves, then export the ledger or a visual report. The exact compared configuration can be passed to a wallet based launch and restored from a share link.

timeline.title: Technical proof with an explicit boundary
timeline.narration: Meteora DBC supplies the quote math and launch transactions. We independently checked the scenario state against fifty six executed swaps across eight local pools. Prices, reserves, fees, balances, and transfers matched in integer units. The browser flow also created, bought, sold, refreshed balances, and graduated to DAMM version two. Public Phantom execution remains unverified; the stock balances in these tests are synthetic.

timeline.title: Build around an actual creator workflow
timeline.narration: The next distribution experiment is three to five observed trials with real launch creators or launchpad developers. We will measure whether a report changes their configuration decision. No adoption, revenue, or testimonials are claimed yet. If teams need the comparison inside their own launchpad, an embeddable module is the next product hypothesis. Public wallet evidence and those user trials are the immediate priorities.
